summary: This lecture continues the story of the Prophet Muhammad SAW in the village of Banu Sa'd with his wet nurse Halimah and foster sister Shaimah, up to the event of the two angels opening his chest. Halimah was frightened and sent him home to Aminah in Mecca when he was about four. Aminah took him and Ummu Aiman to visit Abdullah's grave in Yathrib, but on the way home Aminah fell ill and died at Al-Abwa' when he was six. He was cared for by Ummu Aiman and his grandfather Abdul Muttalib, who died when he was eight, and then he lived with his uncle Abu Talib. The ustaz closes by noting how the Prophet, as an orphan, was tested one trial after another.
keyPoints: Hamzah RA was the Prophet's uncle, the same age as him, and also his foster brother.
The Prophet SAW grew up in a Bedouin tent, close to nature, with his foster sister Shaimah.
Two angels opened his chest, removed a black part and washed his heart with zamzam water, and Anas ibn Malik RA saw the stitch marks.
Halimah was afraid of being blamed and sent him back to Aminah when he was about four.
Aminah died at Al-Abwa' on the way back from Yathrib when he was six, and Ummu Aiman cared for him.
Abdul Muttalib died when he was eight, and he was entrusted to Abu Talib.

chapters.title: Opening
chapters.summary: The ustaz gives thanks for good health and continues the story of the Prophet SAW after his birth.

chapters.title: Hamzah, uncle and foster brother
chapters.summary: The ustaz corrects himself: Hamzah was the Prophet's uncle, the same age as him, and was also nursed by Thuwaibah and Halimah.

chapters.title: Shaimah, the Prophet's foster sister
chapters.summary: Shaimah carried him as a child, and decades later came to meet him, with a bite scar on her back as proof.

chapters.title: Meeting Halimah again
chapters.summary: The Prophet SAW honoured the very old Halimah by spreading out his cloak for her, and some sirah writers say Halimah embraced Islam.

chapters.title: Why babies were sent to the countryside
chapters.summary: Life in Mecca was hard because of disease, while the countryside offered clean air and water and pure Arabic.

chapters.title: Life in a tent, close to nature
chapters.summary: A Bedouin tent was very simple, and the Prophet SAW grew up playing outside until evening, close to nature.

chapters.title: Staying longer in Banu Sa'd
chapters.summary: Halimah asked to keep him longer because of the blessing, and Aminah agreed because she feared disease in Mecca.

chapters.title: Two men in white and the opening of his chest
chapters.summary: While he was playing with his sister and friends, two men in white laid him down and opened his chest.

chapters.title: The black part and the stitch marks
chapters.summary: The angel removed a black part from his heart, washed it with zamzam water and stitched his chest, and Anas RA saw the mark.

chapters.title: Halimah is afraid and sends him home
chapters.summary: The other children ran to tell Halimah, who feared being blamed, so she and her husband Al-Harith decided to send him home.

chapters.title: Back in Mecca and Aminah's words
chapters.summary: He returned to a noisy Mecca. Aminah said he was special, and that she felt no pain while carrying him.

chapters.title: Visiting Abdullah's grave in Yathrib
chapters.summary: Aminah, Ummu Aiman and four-year-old Muhammad joined a caravan to Yathrib and met the Banu Najjar family.

chapters.title: Aminah dies at Al-Abwa'
chapters.summary: On the way home Aminah fell ill at Al-Abwa', entrusted him to Ummu Aiman, and died before the eyes of the six-year-old.

chapters.title: The Prophet SAW weeps at his mother's grave
chapters.summary: Around the age of 60, he wept uncontrollably at his mother's grave in front of the companions.

chapters.title: Cared for by Ummu Aiman and Abdul Muttalib
chapters.summary: Ummu Aiman cared for him like a mother, and the old, blind Abdul Muttalib gave him a special place on his seat.

chapters.title: Abdul Muttalib dies and he lives with Abu Talib
chapters.summary: Abdul Muttalib died when he was eight and entrusted him to Abu Talib, who was poor and had many children.

books.context: A summary of the sirah covering the nursing, the opening of the chest, Aminah's death and Abdul Muttalib.

Entrusted with his care by Abdul Muttalib even though he was poor with many children.
Mentioned as one of his uncles.

people.role: Uncle and foster brother of the Prophet SAW
people.context: The same age as the Prophet SAW and nursed by Thuwaibah and Halimah in Banu Sa'd.

people.role: Wet nurse of the Prophet SAW
people.context: Came from Banu Sa'd, cared for him until about four, and he honoured her when she was very old.

people.role: Foster sister of the Prophet SAW
people.context: Carried him as a child, and came to meet him again with a bite scar on her back as proof.
Halimah told him that the baby should be sent home.
The ustaz says the angel who opened his chest was Jibril, who came in the form of a man.
Saw the stitch marks on the Prophet's chest.
Took him back, brought him to Yathrib, fell ill at Al-Abwa' and died.

people.role: Slave woman and foster mother of the Prophet SAW
people.context: Accompanied Aminah and him, cared for him after Aminah died, and he called her mother.
Died before Aminah could take him to his grave in Yathrib.

people.role: Great-grandmother of the Prophet SAW from Yathrib
people.context: Her children's family, Banu Najjar, was the Prophet's grandmother's family.
One of the companions with the Prophet SAW at Al-Abwa' who wept with him.
Cared for him after Aminah died and gave him a seat of honour, then died and entrusted him to Abu Talib.

sirah.era: From nursing to losing both parents
sirah.summary: This lecture covers the Prophet's life in Banu Sa'd, the opening of his chest, his return to Aminah, Aminah's death at Al-Abwa' and Abdul Muttalib's death, up to his living with Abu Talib.

events.title: His foster sister carries him
events.desc: Shaimah carried him about, tended the goats and watched the sunset with him.

events.label: Two men
events.title: Two men in white come
events.desc: While he played, two men in white seized him and laid him down.

events.label: Chest opened
events.title: His chest is opened
events.desc: The angel removed a black part from his heart and washed it with zamzam water.

events.label: Sent home
events.title: Halimah sends him home
events.desc: Halimah feared being blamed and sent him to Aminah when he was about four.

events.label: Yathrib

lessons.title: Nature calms children
lessons.body: The ustaz says children who spend more time with nature are calmer and more patient than those who are always with screens and games.

lessons.title: Honouring your wet nurse
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW spread out his cloak for the very old Halimah and asked her to sit.

lessons.title: Honouring those who served you
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW gave his foster sister Shaimah a special gift to honour her.

lessons.title: The trust of looking after someone else's child
lessons.body: Halimah was afraid because she would be the one blamed if anything happened to the child in her care.

lessons.title: The Prophet's heart was purified
lessons.body: The angel removed the black part that everyone has, then washed his heart and put it back.

lessons.title: Visiting the graves of parents
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW asked Allah's permission to visit his mother's grave and wept as he remembered her.

lessons.title: Patience through trial after trial
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW was an orphan from birth, lost his mother at six and his grandfather at eight.

lessons.title: A foster mother's love
lessons.body: Ummu Aiman cared for the Prophet SAW like a mother until he called her mother.

lessons.title: A grandfather's love for his grandson
lessons.body: Abdul Muttalib gave his grandson a special place on a seat that no one else could sit on.

lessons.title: Accepting the trust of raising an orphan
lessons.body: Abdul Muttalib entrusted Muhammad to Abu Talib, who was poor and had many children but still looked after him.

glossary.meaning: Village Arabs who lived in tents, unlike city life in Mecca.
Children nursed by the same woman, such as Hamzah and Shaimah with the Prophet SAW.
The Arab tribe of Mecca. The village children called the Prophet SAW the Quraysh boy.
The family of Salma's children in Yathrib, the family of the Prophet's grandmother.
A caravan rest stop halfway between Madinah and Mecca, where Aminah died and was buried.
A woman who raises a child like a mother, as Ummu Aiman did for the Prophet SAW.
Visiting a grave to remember and pray for the deceased.

dalil.translation: The Prophet SAW related that his chest was opened and his heart washed, and Anas ibn Malik RA said he had seen the stitch marks on his chest.
dalil.context: The ustaz presents this as the words of the Prophet SAW and names Anas ibn Malik as his attendant. He does not name the source book.

dalil.translation: The Prophet SAW said he asked Allah's permission to visit his mother's grave and Allah gave it, then he wept until the companions wept too.
dalil.context: The ustaz tells this when the Prophet SAW was with Umar RA and the companions at Al-Abwa'. He does not name the narrator or source.
